title: Can a local mean-field predict which robot blocks tip a ring crowd's passing-side convention?
lede: A deterministic local mean-field agrees with the society-allies simulation on tip/no-tip in 141 of 160 cells but is not a bound in either direction: it overstates the share of evenly spread robots needed (0.20 against 0.12 at k = 2) and tips at or below the simulation for blocks of 4 to 8.
summary: A fixed-point map for the ring walking-side game (one number per person, memory slots as independent draws, N = 200, M = 9, ε = 0.02) is compared with the society-allies simulation over 160 cells (robot share 0.04–0.40, blocks 1/2/4/8, neighbourhood k = 1/2/3/5, 10 seeds). It matches the simulated tip/no-tip outcome in 141 cells; in 11 of the other 19 the simulation tips and the map does not, in 8 the reverse. It reproduces the rise of the threshold with block size and its fall with k, puts the spread-robot threshold at 0.20 against 0.12 simulated, and for blocks of 4 and 8 at k ≥ 2 tips at or below the simulation (below in 5 of 6 cells), partly a horizon effect. Corrected 2026-11-19: an earlier version's 1/1000 binomial lookup froze slow fronts. Limits: stylised 1D binary game with chosen M and ε; the cause of the gap (finite-size noise or the memory-independence step) is not tested; thresholds are coarse (±0.04).
